subject: Hosted API: monthly token runway, peak QPS sanity check and budget clarification
messages:
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Sienna Morales <sienna@clearline.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Sun, 14 Mar 2026 15:12:00 -0700
Subject: Hosted API: monthly token runway, peak QPS sanity check and budget clarification

Hi Sienna —

Great to connect earlier. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored hosted pricing note for Clearline:

1) Current baseline and ramp
- You mentioned ~2.8M tokens/month on the pilot (prod traffic today).
- Planned rollouts: ramp to ~18M tokens/month over ~6 months (marketing + user invite waves).

2) Burst / concurrency shape
- Onboarding bursts: brief spikes up to ~65 TPS (observed during last test).
- Sustained 99th percentile we should use for sizing: you estimated ~48 TPS.

3) Budget and unit target
- You indicated a monthly budget range of $7k–$12k for inference initially.
- Target unit economics goal you called out: roughly $8–$10 / 1M tokens.

Action items I need from you to confirm our hosted proposal:
- Please fill the attached forecast-template.xlsx (month-by-month tokens, expected peak-minute TPS, and any canary regions).
- If finance prefers a single contact, copy finance@clearline.ai in the reply (we can lead with a simple SOW/PO route).

Attachments: forecast-template.xlsx (simple monthly columnar template)

If those ranges are still accurate I’ll draft a 90-day pilot pricing note with two bands (commit vs. on-demand) and a burst allowance for onboarding spikes.

Thanks — talk soon.

— Markus
Markus Klein
Head of Sales — Enterprise
Redwood Inference
markus.klein@redwood.com | +1 415 555 0123

From: Sienna Morales <sienna@clearline.ai>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
Cc: Clearline Finance <finance@clearline.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2026 09:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Hosted API: monthly token runway, peak QPS sanity check and budget clarification

Markus —

Thanks for the summary and the template. Attached is our raw usage export and a quick note from finance. Quick clarifications inline:

- Baseline today: 2.8M tokens/mo (production reads + small write path).
- Ramp: aggressive plan is 18M by month 6; conservative plan is 10M by month 6 — we prioritize MAU growth but want cost predictability.
- Peak behavior: onboarding test generated a ~65 TPS spike for ~3 minutes, normal peak minute is ~38–45 TPS, 99th ~48 TPS sounds right.
- Budget: finance gave us a $7k–$12k window to support the ramp; total platform budget includes telemetry/DB costs.
- Unit target: ideally $8 / 1M; finance would accept up to $10/1M if we get clear burst protection and a predictable overage model.

Attachments: clearline-usage-export.csv

Two asks for Redwood:
1) Can you show an example monthly invoice math for the 10M and 18M scenarios with a burst allowance (e.g., 10% burst buffer and separate 1-hour onboarding burst credit)?
2) SOC2 summary + data residency note (we're in the US, but security needs to sign off).

I'll loop in procurement if you can give a SOW/PO starter.

Best,
Sienna Morales
Head of Platform
Clearline Health
sienna@clearline.ai

On Sun, Mar 14, 2026 at 3:12 PM Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com> wrote:
> Hi Sienna —
> 
> Great to connect earlier. Quick recap + a couple of asks so we can put together a tailored hosted pricing note for Clearline: [trimmed for thread]
From: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 16 Mar 2026 10:22:00 -07:00
Subject: Fwd: Hosted API: monthly token runway, peak QPS sanity check and budget clarification — pricing approach

Marissa / Karthik —

Forwarding Sienna's reply and usage export. Highlights: Clearline expects a 10–18M token runway (conservative vs aggressive) and short blasts up to ~65 TPS during onboarding; finance wants $7k–$12k/mo and target ~$8/1M.

Suggested approach for the hosted note:
- Build two scenario rows (10M, 18M) with two pricing bands: committed-monthly discount vs on-demand.
- Offer a short onboarding burst credit (one 1-hour credit sized at 2x baseline TPS) and a 10% monthly burst buffer for auto-scaling tolerance.
- Put $/1M at $9 baseline for the committed band (midpoint of their target), with an overage tier at $11/1M. On-demand band at $13/1M.

Questions:
- Marissa: is $9/1M + 10% burst buffer defensible given our current unit economics and the model quantization profiles they'd likely use?
- Karthik: any concerns about SLOs if we carve the burst credit the way I described (shouldn't impact 99th P99 SLO for other customers)?

I'll draft the two-scenario spreadsheet and the short SOW (PO-friendly) — aim to send to Sienna by EOD tomorrow if we agree.

— Markus

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Markus Klein <markus.klein@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 17 Mar 2026 11:04:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Fwd: Hosted API: monthly token runway, peak QPS sanity check and budget clarification — pricing approach

Markus / Karthik —

I like the two-scenario framing. A couple of notes:
- $9/1M as a committed midpoint is fine operationally (we can recommend a 3–6 month commit with monthly true-ups).
- Make the onboarding credit explicit in the SOW: one 1-hour window at up to 2x their observed spike (so cover the 65 TPS test) and then auto-throttle/notify if sustained beyond that.
- Karthik: please confirm capacity safety net for week-0 onboarding so we don't evict other low-priority batches. If that looks good I'll OK the doc.

Assuming approvals, next steps:
1) Markus: send the draft pricing note + simple SOW to Sienna and cc finance@clearline.ai.
2) Karthik: prepare a one-page ops note on canary routing and burst handling to attach.
3) I'll prepare standard PO/SOW language for procurement.

Thanks — Marissa
